# Disclosure timing is not fact coverage: a Trickle Test diagnostic
## TL;DR
On a fixed annotated dialogue corpus, preserving the number of facts revealed at every turn does not preserve which facts are revealed. We processed two 128-dialogue shards of Google's Schema-Guided Dialogue (SGD), with 124 eligible test dialogues, 746 user turns and 391 first-INFORM facts. SGD uses simulated dialogue outlines paraphrased by crowd workers: this is a metric diagnostic, not spontaneous human behavior or a Persimmon run.
![Measured disclosure timing and cumulative recall](/assets/research/manager-disclosure-timing-2026-11-27.svg)

## Method
A fact is a normalized (service, slot, canonical value) from a USER INFORM action. Compare the actual first-occurrence schedule with oracle schedules revealing all facts first, last, or shuffling fact identities across the same disclosure times (five seeds). No model calls; no data training.
## Results
| Schedule | Strict first-event F1 | Cumulative recall | Timing MAE (turns) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Reference | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.000 |
| All first | 0.322 | 1.000 | 1.598 |
| All last | 0.000 | 0.205 | 3.867 |
| Shuffle (5-seed mean) | 0.510 | 0.893 | 1.038 |
Every schedule covers the same eventual fact set. Shuffle preserves the cumulative count curve exactly. Yet fact-level temporal matching falls to 51%. Normal and optimized Python receipts are identical. Dialogue bootstrap (2000 draws) first-minus-last strict F1 95% interval [0.267,0.375], conditional on these samples and oracle schedules.
## Limits and implications
These are our proxies, not the official Trickle Test or model quality. Official Persimmon access and original evaluation episodes remain unavailable. User privacy and consent are prerequisites; do not optimize for extracting sensitive disclosures. ManagerBench should distinguish timing, fact identity, and permission. No training, deployment or human efficacy claim.
